verdictRationale: `verify 1` was owed and ran inside the loop, attributed to M2@K1 (TRG-001) and M1@K1 (TRG-002), both on the `auth` surface — so the safeguard family is credential/enforcement, not persistence or contract. Every enforcement claim in the contract is covered by an executed test (all five `/tasks` routes × missing key and × wrong key, auth-before-existence, auth-before-validation, no-mutation-on-reject, public root, default key accepted, configured key replaces the default). Build 0/0 and 21/21 tests were re-run independently after the last code change. Not clean READY: three findings are carried as accepted debt rather than fixed here — the posture document now contradicts the delivered behaviour, and the committed default credential plus the non-constant-time comparison are deliberately out of scope per ADR-001.
commentary: `review 1` (fired by M4/TRG-003) is a focused review folded into this verify pass, per design §4 — a standalone review pass is owed only at `review 2`, which nothing fired. No `openspec` check row is reported because the `openspec` CLI is not installed here and the record's only vocabulary for that row is PASS/FAIL, which would assert a command that never ran. The post-authoring drift check was done by reading: every scenario in `openspec/changes/require-api-key-auth/specs/task-api/spec.md` maps to an executed test, so the depth-1 delta spec and the delivered behaviour agree. `openspec status` would read `isComplete: false` at depth 1 by design — it measures the FULL set.

findings.title: `.chaos/architecture.md` now contradicts the delivered behaviour
findings.detail: Refs TRG-002 (M1 posture-crossing, surface auth). The posture doc still reads "Authentication / authorization posture — None. The API is open." and lists auth under Non-goals, while `/tasks` is now closed. The crossing itself is approved (PROP-DEC-001) and recorded (ADR-001); what remains is the document.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile the posture document via `chaos:sync` at archive. This run may not silently rewrite repository posture docs, so it is carried as debt rather than fixed here

findings.title: A working default credential is committed to the repository
findings.detail: Refs TRG-001 (M2 sensitive-surface, surface auth). `ApiKeyEndpointFilter.DefaultApiKey = "test-secret-key"` means an unconfigured deployment ships with a publicly known key. The change contract mandates exactly this default, and ADR-001 accepts it as a demo risk (RK-3).
findings.recommendation: If this API is ever hosted, make `ApiKey` a required configuration value and fail startup when it is absent

findings.title: Key comparison is ordinal, not constant-time
findings.detail: Refs TRG-001 (M2 sensitive-surface, surface auth). `string.Equals(..., StringComparison.Ordinal)` short-circuits, so it is theoretically timing-distinguishable. ADR-001 puts hashing/constant-time comparison explicitly out of scope; confidence is MEDIUM because the practical exploitability over HTTP against an in-memory demo is not measured, only reasoned.
findings.recommendation: Use `CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals` over the UTF-8 bytes if this ever guards a real credential
